claim: In humans, there are three HP1 paralogs: HP1α, HP1β, and HP1γ.
source: In humans, there are three paralogs, HP1α, HP1β, and HP1γ, which exhibit remarkable similarities in their domain architecture and sequence properties.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and introduction of the manuscript.

claim: HP1 paralogs exhibit distinct behaviors in liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS).
source: Nevertheless, these paralogs display distinct behaviors in liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS), a process linked to heterochromatin formation.
evidence: This is a central claim of the manuscript supported by computational simulations and referenced experimental data.

claim: Net charge and charge patterning along the sequence govern HP1 paralog LLPS propensities.
source: We highlight the significance of the net charge and charge patterning along the sequence in governing paralog LLPS propensities.
evidence: This claim is supported by the coarse-grained simulation data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Both highly conserved folded domains and less-conserved disordered domains contribute to the observed differences in HP1 paralog LLPS.
source: We also show that both highly conserved folded and less-conserved disordered domains contribute to the observed differences.
evidence: This is supported by domain-swapping simulation experiments described in the manuscript.

claim: DNA can significantly reshape the stability of a minimal condensate formed by HP1 paralogs due to competitive interactions.
source: Importantly, our study reveals that DNA can significantly reshape the stability of a minimal condensate formed by HP1 paralogs due to competitive interactions of HP1α with HP1β and HP1γ versus DNA.
evidence: This is demonstrated through coarse-grained simulations with DNA presented in the manuscript.

claim: HP1 paralogs are encoded by chromobox (CBX) genes: CBX5 for HP1α, CBX1 for HP1β, and CBX3 for HP1γ.
source: In humans, the HP1 family comprises three paralogs, HP1α, HP1β, and HP1γ, encoded by a class of genes known as the chromobox (CBX) genes (CBX5, CBX1, and CBX3, respectively).
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction.

claim: All three HP1 paralogs localize to heterochromatic regions where they mediate chromatin condensation and gene silencing.
source: All three paralogs localize to heterochromatic regions where they mediate chromatin condensation and gene silencing (Zeng et al., 2010; Larson and Narlikar, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by cited references.

claim: HP1β and HP1γ have been found in euchromatic regions that express active genes.
source: However, HP1β and HP1γ have also been found in euchromatic regions that express active genes (Eissenberg and Elgin, 2000; Hediger and Gasser, 2006; Kwon and Workman, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by cited references.

claim: HP1 proteins have potential association with cancer development.
source: The importance of HP1 proteins in genome regulation and their potential association with cancer development (Jeon et al., 2022) has prompted increasing endeavors to elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying their biological activity.
evidence: This is supported by a cited reference.

claim: HP1 paralogs possess a basic structure consisting of two highly conserved folded domains (CD and CSD), connected by a disordered hinge and two unstructured N and C terminal extensions (NTE and CTE).
source: They possess a basic structure that consists of two highly conserved folded domains, the chromodomain (CD) and the chromoshadow domain (CSD), connected by a disordered hinge of variable lengths and two unstructured N and C terminal extensions (NTE and CTE, respectively).
evidence: This is a well-established structural description of HP1 proteins.

claim: The chromodomain (CD) specifically recognizes methylated lysine 9 on the histone H3 tail (H3K9me), an epigenetic mark for gene silencing.
source: The CD specifically recognizes methylated lysine 9 on the histone H3 tail (H3K9me), an epigenetic mark for gene silencing (Lachner et al., 2001; Bannister et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by cited references.

claim: The chromoshadow domain (CSD) mediates the dimerization of HP1 and interacts with other proteins through a PXVXL motif.
source: The CSD mediates the dimerization of HP1 and interacts with other proteins through a PXVXL motif (Cowieson et al., 2000; Smothers and Henikoff, 2000; Thiru et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by cited references.

claim: Dissociation constant (Kd) values in the nano-molar range have been reported for CSD homodimerization of HP1α and HP1β.
source: Dissociation constant (Kd) values in the nano-molar range have been reported for CSD homodimerization of HP1α and HP1β (Her et al., 2022; Brasher et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by cited references.

claim: Mammalian HP1 paralogs can form heterodimers directly with one another.
source: Moreover, in vitro and in vivo co-immunoprecipitation have shown that mammalian HP1 paralogs can form heterodimers directly with one another (Nielsen et al., 2001), which raises the question of the biological functions of these heterodimers.
evidence: This is supported by a cited reference.

claim: The hinge region has been observed to target HP1 to heterochromatic regions through non-specific binding to DNA and RNA.
source: The hinge region has been observed to target HP1 to heterochromatic regions through non-specific binding to DNA and RNA (Keenen et al., 2021; Muchardt et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by cited references.

claim: Interactions between the hinge region and the CTE are proposed to be responsible for an auto-inhibited dimer conformation.
source: Furthermore, interactions between the hinge region and the CTE are proposed to be responsible for an auto-inhibited dimer conformation (Larson et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a cited reference.

claim: The NTE has been implicated in mediating the binding affinity of the CD for the methylated histone H3 tail.
source: By contrast, the NTE has been implicated in mediating the binding affinity of the CD for the methylated histone H3 tail (Canzio et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a cited reference.

claim: HP1α can undergo LLPS upon either NTE phosphorylation (pHP1α) or DNA binding.
source: However, in vitro experiments have shown that HP1α can undergo LLPS upon either NTE phosphorylation (pHP1α) or DNA binding, which provides a new perspective on heterochromatin formation and function through a phase-separation mechanism (Keenen et al., 2021; Larson et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by cited references.

claim: HP1α can undergo LLPS at high protein concentrations and low salt concentrations without phosphorylation or DNA binding.
source: Without phosphorylation or DNA binding, HP1α can undergo LLPS at high protein concentrations (Keenen et al., 2021; Qin et al., 2021) and low salt concentrations (Wang et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by cited references.

claim: HP1γ undergoes LLPS at a protein concentration that is multi-fold higher than the threshold concentration for HP1α.
source: While HP1γ undergoes LLPS at a protein concentration that is multi-fold higher than the threshold concentration for HP1α (Qin et al., 2021), HP1β does not form liquid droplets under any tested conditions (Larson et al., 2017; Qin et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by cited references.

claim: HP1β does not form liquid droplets under any tested conditions.
source: While HP1γ undergoes LLPS at a protein concentration that is multi-fold higher than the threshold concentration for HP1α (Qin et al., 2021), HP1β does not form liquid droplets under any tested conditions (Larson et al., 2017; Qin et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by cited references.

claim: HP1β, but not HP1α or HP1γ, can form liquid-like droplets in the presence of histone proteins.
source: However, HP1β, but not HP1α or HP1γ, can form liquid-like droplets in the presence of histone proteins (Qin et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a cited reference.

claim: The NTE, hinge, and CTE of HP1β share 35%, 33%, and 38% sequence similarity with the corresponding regions of HP1α, respectively.
source: Compared to the corresponding regions of HP1α, the NTE, hinge, and CTE of HP1β share 35%, 33%, and 38% sequence similarity, respectively, while for HP1γ those numbers are 15%, 36%, and 19%, respectively (Canzio et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a cited reference.

claim: The NTE, hinge, and CTE of HP1γ share 15%, 36%, and 19% sequence similarity with the corresponding regions of HP1α, respectively.
source: Compared to the corresponding regions of HP1α, the NTE, hinge, and CTE of HP1β share 35%, 33%, and 38% sequence similarity, respectively, while for HP1γ those numbers are 15%, 36%, and 19%, respectively (Canzio et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a cited reference.

claim: The CD and CSD domains of HP1α and HP1β show over 80% sequence similarity.
source: On the other hand, the CD and CSD domains of HP1α and HP1β show over 80% sequence similarity, while the similarities between these domains in HP1α and HP1γ are 71% and 87%, respectively (Canzio et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a cited reference.

claim: The similarities between CD and CSD domains in HP1α and HP1γ are 71% and 87%, respectively.
source: On the other hand, the CD and CSD domains of HP1α and HP1β show over 80% sequence similarity, while the similarities between these domains in HP1α and HP1γ are 71% and 87%, respectively (Canzio et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a cited reference.

claim: The CD and CSD are both globular domains that consist of three anti-parallel β-strands at the N-terminus and an α-helix at the C-terminus.
source: They consist of three anti-parallel β-strands at the N-terminus and an α-helix at the C-terminus.
evidence: This is a structural description based on known structures.

claim: The structural difference between the monomeric units of CD and CSD can be attributed to the presence of an additional α-helix in the CSD.
source: The structural difference between the monomeric units of CD and CSD can be attributed to the presence of an additional α-helix in the CSD (Figure 1b).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1b.

claim: The CD functions as a monomer while the CSD forms a symmetrical homodimer.
source: It should be noted that the CD functions as a monomer while the CSD forms a symmetrical homodimer where the two CSD monomers interact via their α-helices (Figure 1c).
evidence: This is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 1c.

claim: HP1 paralogs are enriched in charged residues, with Arg, Lys, Glu, and Asp comprising 39–45% of the total number of amino acids in the protein.
source: HP1 paralogs are enriched in charged residues, with Arg, Lys, Glu, and Asp comprising 39–45% of the total number of amino acids in the protein.
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: HP1β has the highest percentage of charged residues (45%), with a predominance of negatively charged amino acids (26%).
source: Of the three paralogs, HP1β has the highest percentage of charged residues (45%), with a predominance of negatively charged amino acids (26%).
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: HP1β has a net charge of –13, which is more negative than the net charge of HP1γ (–5) and HP1α (–3).
source: This results in a net charge of –13, which is more negative than the net charge of HP1γ (–5) and HP1α (–3).
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: HP1β has the lowest isoelectric point (pI 4.85), followed by HP1γ (pI 5.13) and HP1α (pI 5.71).
source: Ion-exchange chromatography also showed that HP1β has the lowest isoelectric point (pI 4.85), followed by HP1γ (pI 5.13) and HP1α (pI 5.71) (Qin et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a cited reference.

claim: The HP1α NTE has a unique block of four serine residues that are constitutively phosphorylated in vivo.
source: It is important to note that the HP1α NTE has a unique block of four serine residues (Figure 1a) that are constitutively phosphorylated in vivo (Hiragami-Hamada et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the text, shown in Figure 1a, and supported by a cited reference.

claim: Phosphorylation can dramatically change the charge on the HP1α NTE and significantly reduce the minimum concentration required for LLPS in the absence of DNA.
source: Phosphorylation can dramatically change the charge on the HP1α NTE and significantly reduce the minimum concentration required for LLPS in the absence of DNA (Her et al., 2022; Larson et al., 2017; Hiragami-Hamada et al., 2011; Nishibuchi et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by cited references.

claim: HP1β conformations are on average more extended than HP1α and HP1γ structures.
source: We found that the HP1β conformations (Rg = 3.93 ± 0.78) are on average more extended than the HP1α and HP1γ structures (Rg = 3.20 ± 0.31 nm and Rg = 3.48 ± 0.69 nm, respectively), which is consistent with observations in previous work (Larson et al., 2017; Munari et al., 2013; Latham and Zhang, 2021).
evidence: This is based on coarse-grained simulation data and supported by cited references.

claim: The average dimension of HP1 paralogs expands in order of increasing the net negative charge of the respective homodimer.
source: Notably, the average dimension of HP1 paralogs expands in order of increasing the net negative charge of the respective homodimer where HP1α has a negative charge q = –6, HP1γ has q = –10, and HP1β has q = –26.
evidence: This is based on coarse-grained simulation data presented in the manuscript.

claim: HP1β has the smallest number of contacts at the domain level among the three paralogs, presumably due to charge repulsion between extended stretches of acidic residues in its domains.
source: Among the three paralogs, HP1β has the smallest number of contacts at the domain level, presumably due to charge repulsion between extended stretches of acidic residues in its domains.
evidence: This is based on contact analysis from coarse-grained simulations.

claim: The hinge and CTE of HP1α are much more interaction-prone in both monomer and dimer contexts compared to HP1β and HP1γ.
source: While HP1α and HP1γ make similar contacts with their folded domains, the hinge and CTE of HP1α are much more interaction-prone in both monomer and dimer contexts.
evidence: This is based on contact analysis from coarse-grained simulations.

claim: HP1β did not undergo phase separation in CG coexistence simulations, while HP1α and HP1γ formed stable condensates.
source: Under the simulation conditions, HP1β did not undergo phase separation, while HP1α and HP1γ formed stable condensates (as evidenced in the flat density profiles in Figure 2f and snapshots in Figure 2g; Figure 2—video 2), but the Csat of HP1γ was approximately twofold higher than that of HP1α (inset of Figure 2f).
evidence: This is demonstrated by coarse-grained simulation data shown in Figure 2f and 2g.

claim: The Csat of HP1γ was approximately twofold higher than that of HP1α in CG coexistence simulations.
source: Under the simulation conditions, HP1β did not undergo phase separation, while HP1α and HP1γ formed stable condensates (as evidenced in the flat density profiles in Figure 2f and snapshots in Figure 2g; Figure 2—video 2), but the Csat of HP1γ was approximately twofold higher than that of HP1α (inset of Figure 2f).
evidence: This is demonstrated by coarse-grained simulation data shown in Figure 2f.

claim: The critical temperature (or the phase separation propensity) decreased in order for HP1α, HP1γ, and HP1β.
source: We also constructed the phase diagrams for HP1 paralogs and found that the critical temperature (or the phase separation propensity) decreased in order for HP1α, HP1γ, and HP1β (Figure 2h).
evidence: This is demonstrated by phase diagram data shown in Figure 2h.

claim: NTE-hinge interactions and NTE-NTE interactions govern the conformation of HP1 paralogs in the dilute state and drive multivalency under crowding conditions.
source: In summary, NTE-hinge interactions and NTE-NTE (between the charge-segregated diblocks) interactions govern the conformation of HP1 paralogs in the dilute state and drive multivalency under crowding conditions.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the simulation data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Substantial interactions between disordered segments (NTE, hinge, and CTE) and folded domains (CD and CSD) highlight the positive role of folded domains in the condensate formation of HP1 paralogs.
source: Additionally, substantial interactions between disordered segments (NTE, hinge, and CTE) and folded domains (CD and CSD) highlight the positive role of folded domains in the condensate formation of HP1 paralogs (Figure 3a).
evidence: This is based on contact analysis from coarse-grained simulations shown in Figure 3a.

claim: HP1α chimeras with IDRs replaced with those from HP1β or HP1γ are less prone to phase separation compared to wild-type HP1α.
source: We found that the HP1β or HP1γ IDRs fail to enhance inter-dimer NTE-hinge interactions. These chimeras are less prone to phase separation compared to the wild-type HP1α (Figure 3b and c).
evidence: This is demonstrated by coarse-grained simulation data shown in Figures 3b and 3c.

claim: HP1α chimeras with the hinge replaced with the hinge from HP1β or HP1γ did not form stable condensates.
source: We found that neither of the chimeras formed stable condensates (Figure 3d and e).
evidence: This is demonstrated by coarse-grained simulation data shown in Figures 3d and 3e.

claim: The positively charged lysine/arginine residue clusters in the HP1α hinge are necessary to induce inter-dimer contacts for condensate formation.
source: Taken together, these results demonstrate that the positively charged lysine/arginine residue clusters in the HP1α hinge are necessary to induce inter-dimer contacts for condensate formation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from domain-swapping simulation experiments.

claim: HP1β-αHinge chimera displayed Csat that was lower than that for wild-type HP1α, and comparable to the Csat of pHP1α.
source: The HP1β-αHinge chimera displayed Csat that was lower than that for wild-type HP1α, and that was comparable to the Csat of pHP1α, which is much more prone to phase separation (Her et al., 2022).
evidence: This is demonstrated by coarse-grained simulation data and comparison with previous work.

claim: HP1γ-αHinge showed a Csat nearly threefold lower compared to pHP1α.
source: HP1γ-αHinge showed an even more remarkable reduction in the Csat, which was nearly threefold lower compared to pHP1α (Figure 3e).
evidence: This is demonstrated by coarse-grained simulation data shown in Figure 3e.

claim: HP1α chimeras with folded domains replaced with those from HP1β or HP1γ readily formed stable condensates with Csat values lower than wild-type HP1α and comparable to pHP1α.
source: Intriguingly, we again observed that both chimeras readily formed stable condensates, and their Csat values were lower than the concentration for HP1α and comparable to the concentration for pHP1α (Figure 3g and h).
evidence: This is demonstrated by coarse-grained simulation data shown in Figures 3g and 3h.

claim: Swapping the CD domain alone from either HP1β or HP1γ into HP1α substantially enhanced interactions between the hinge and the folded domains and reduced competing CTE contacts, promoting phase separation more efficiently.
source: We found that swapping the CD domain alone (from either HP1β or HP1γ) substantially enhanced interactions between the hinge and the folded domains and reduced competing CTE contacts, hence promoting phase separation more efficiently.
evidence: This is demonstrated by coarse-grained simulation data from domain-swapping experiments.

claim: The CD domains of HP1β and HP1γ contain more negatively charged residues with a larger solvent-accessible surface area (SASA) than HP1α.
source: Despite sharing high sequence identity and domain architecture similarity, the CD domains of HP1β and HP1γ contain more negatively charged residues with a larger solvent-accessible surface area (SASA) than HP1α (Figure 3—figure supplement 1f and g).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1f and g.

claim: The CD domain is more dominant than the CSD in influencing the inter-domain interactions that drive phase separation.
source: Therefore, our data suggest that the CD domain is more dominant than the CSD in influencing the inter-domain interactions that drive phase separation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from domain-swapping simulation experiments.

claim: The condensate formation of HP1 mainly relies on NTE-hinge interactions, but the folded domains, particularly the CD domain, also substantially contribute to the multivalent interactions required for phase separation.
source: Taken together, our findings reveal the cooperative roles of disordered and folded domains in mediating the condensation behavior of HP1 paralogs. While the condensate formation of HP1 mainly relies on NTE-hinge interactions, the folded domains, particularly the CD domain, also substantially contribute to the multivalent interactions required for the formation of oligomeric networks and phase separation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from domain-swapping simulation experiments.

claim: The CSD-CSD dimerization of HP1α occurs with an estimated Kd in the nanomolar range.
source: Previous literature has shown that the CSD-CSD dimerization of HP1α occurs with an estimated Kd in the nanomolar range (Her et al., 2022; Brasher et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by cited references.

claim: The CSDs of HP1 paralogs exhibit a high degree of homology, suggesting that heterodimerization is likely to occur.
source: Moreover, the CSDs of HP1 paralogs exhibit a high degree of homology, suggesting that heterodimerization is likely to occur.
evidence: This is an inference based on sequence homology.

claim: HP1αβ, HP1αγ, and HP1βγ heterodimers formed stable condensates in CG coexistence simulations.
source: We found that the three heterodimers formed stable condensates (Figure 4a and b).
evidence: This is demonstrated by coarse-grained simulation data shown in Figures 4a and 4b.

claim: The Csat for HP1αβ and HP1αγ heterodimers were nearly tenfold higher than the concentration for HP1α homodimers.
source: The Csat for HP1αβ and HP1αγ heterodimers were nearly tenfold higher than the concentration for HP1α homodimers, while the Csat of HP1αγ heterodimers was comparable to the concentration of HP1γ homodimers (Figure 4a–c).
evidence: This is demonstrated by coarse-grained simulation data shown in Figures 4a-c.

claim: The presence of either HP1α or HP1γ monomer in heterodimerization with HP1β can induce the necessary inter-dimer interactions in HP1β monomers to sufficiently stabilize the condensed phase.
source: It appears that the presence of either HP1α or HP1γ monomer in heterodimerization with HP1β can induce the necessary inter-dimer interactions in HP1β monomers to sufficiently stabilize the condensed phase (Figure 4e; Figure 4—figure supplement 1a and b).
evidence: This is demonstrated by coarse-grained simulation data shown in Figure 4e and Figure 4—figure supplement 1a and b.

claim: HP1α can interact with DNA via stretches of basic residues located within the hinge region, mediating the bridging of distinct DNA regions and inducing DNA compaction.
source: Recent studies have demonstrated that HP1α can interact with DNA via stretches of basic residues located within the hinge region, mediating the bridging of distinct DNA regions and inducing DNA compaction (Keenen et al., 2021; Larson et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by cited references.

claim: HP1γ has been shown to form condensates with DNA but requires higher protein concentrations to induce droplet formation than HP1α.
source: HP1γ has also been shown to form condensates with DNA but requires higher protein concentrations to induce droplet formation than HP1α (Keenen et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a cited reference.

claim: HP1β did not undergo condensation with DNA under any tested conditions.
source: Conversely, HP1β did not undergo condensation with DNA under any tested conditions (Keenen et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a cited reference.

claim: In CG simulations with DNA, HP1β homodimer did not undergo phase separation, while dsDNA partitioned into and stabilized the condensates of HP1α and HP1γ.
source: We found that the HP1β homodimer did not undergo phase separation, while dsDNA partitioned into and stabilized the condensates of HP1α and HP1γ (Figure 5a and b; Figure 5—video 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by coarse-grained simulation data shown in Figures 5a and 5b.

claim: In the presence of dsDNA, the Csat of HP1γ is approximately twofold higher than that of HP1α.
source: In the presence of dsDNA, the Csat of HP1γ is approximately twofold higher than that of HP1α.
evidence: This is demonstrated by coarse-grained simulation data.

claim: The electrostatic interactions between dsDNA and the lysine/arginine-rich hinge dominated in the HP1α homodimer.
source: We found that the electrostatic interactions between dsDNA and the lysine/arginine-rich hinge dominated in the HP1α homodimer (Figure 5c).
evidence: This is demonstrated by contact analysis from coarse-grained simulations shown in Figure 5c.

claim: dsDNA favored the long stretch of lysine-rich NTE of HP1γ homodimers.
source: dsDNA also favored the long stretch of lysine-rich NTE of HP1γ homodimers (Figure 5e).
evidence: This is demonstrated by contact analysis from coarse-grained simulations shown in Figure 5e.

claim: The electrostatic interactions between dsDNA and HP1β were unfavorable due to extended patches of acidic residues along the HP1β sequence.
source: However, the electrostatic interactions between dsDNA and HP1β were unfavorable due to extended patches of acidic residues along the HP1β sequence (Figure 5d).
evidence: This is demonstrated by contact analysis from coarse-grained simulations shown in Figure 5d.

claim: DNA could induce condensate formation of all HP1 heterodimers.
source: We observed that DNA could induce condensate formation of all HP1 heterodimers (Figure 5f and g).
evidence: This is demonstrated by coarse-grained simulation data shown in Figures 5f and 5g.

claim: HP1β homodimers were predominantly localized towards the periphery of the condensate while HP1α and dsDNA occupied the interior in equimolar HP1α+HP1β mixtures with DNA.
source: We observed that HP1β homodimers were predominantly localized towards the periphery of the condensate while HP1α and dsDNA occupied the interior (Figure 6d and e; Figure 6—video 2).
evidence: This is demonstrated by coarse-grained simulation data shown in Figures 6d and 6e.

claim: HP1γ was able to co-localize and form stable condensates with HP1α and dsDNA.
source: On the other hand, HP1γ was able to co-localize and form stable condensates with HP1α and dsDNA (Figure 6d and f; Figure 6—video 2).
evidence: This is demonstrated by coarse-grained simulation data shown in Figures 6d and 6f.

claim: The HP1β/HP1α homodimer mixtures showed behavior consistent with scaffold-client co-phase separation.
source: We found that the HP1β/HP1α homodimer mixtures showed behavior consistent with scaffold-client co-phase separation (Figure 6b).
evidence: This is demonstrated by multicomponent phase diagram data shown in Figure 6b.

claim: The HP1γ/HP1α homodimer assembly showed behavior consistent with cooperative co-phase separation.
source: In contrast, the HP1γ/HP1α homodimer assembly showed behavior consistent with cooperative co-phase separation (Figure 6c).
evidence: This is demonstrated by multicomponent phase diagram data shown in Figure 6c.

claim: The presence of dsDNA substantially enhanced the phase separation of HP1α but slightly excluded HP1γ from the HP1α-DNA complex.
source: However, compared to the case of mixing HP1α and HP1γ alone, the dilute-phase concentration of HP1γ was found to be twofold higher, whereas the dilute-phase concentration of HP1α was nearly twofold lower. In other words, the presence of dsDNA substantially enhanced the phase separation of HP1α but slightly excluded HP1γ from the HP1α-DNA complex.
evidence: This is demonstrated by multicomponent phase diagram data with DNA.

claim: HP1γ may co-partition in HP1α-DNA condensates while HP1β mostly remains in the condensate boundary.
source: Together, these results suggest that HP1γ may co-partition in HP1α-DNA condensates while HP1β mostly remains in the condensate boundary.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multicomponent simulation data with DNA.

claim: In the absence of DNA, the main driver for LLPS is the relative strength of hinge-NTE interactions.
source: In the absence of DNA, the main driver for LLPS is the relative strength of hinge-NTE interactions.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the simulation data presented in the manuscript.

claim: HP1α has the most positively charged hinge region, which can interact with negatively charged patches on the NTE and the CTE.
source: HP1α, the most LLPS-prone paralog, has the most positively charged hinge region, which can interact with negatively charged patches on the NTE and the CTE.
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis and simulation data.

claim: Competition from the CTE negatively influences the LLPS propensity of wild-type HP1α.
source: While hinge-NTE interactions are dominant, competition from the CTE negatively influences the LLPS propensity of the wild-type protein.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from simulation data.

claim: Phosphorylation of serine residues 11–14 on the NTE significantly enhances LLPS of HP1α.
source: This balance can be shifted dramatically by the phosphorylation of serine residues 11–14 on the NTE, which significantly enhances LLPS (Her et al., 2022; Larson et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by cited references and previous simulation work.

claim: HP1γ and HP1β do not have the phosphorylatable serine patch in their NTEs and therefore lack the ability to tune the strength of hinge-NTE interactions.
source: Importantly, HP1γ and HP1β do not have the phosphorylatable serine patch in their NTEs and, therefore, lack the ability to tune the strength of hinge-NTE interactions.
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis.

claim: Deletion of the HP1α CTE in the context of phosphorylation reduced the Csat tenfold.
source: Deletion of the HP1α CTE in the context of phosphorylation reduced the Csat tenfold, supporting a model where reducing competition from the CTE is key to increasing LLPS propensity.
evidence: This is supported by experimental observations.

claim: The NTE and the CD can work in concert to compete with the CTE for access to the positively charged hinge.
source: This also indicates that the NTE and the CD can work in concert to compete with the CTE for access to the positively charged hinge.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from domain-swapping simulation data.

claim: The CD of HP1 paralogs has a well-established role in recognizing and binding H3K9me2/3, facilitating the targeted recruitment and localization of HP1 to heterochromatic regions.
source: The CD of HP1 paralogs has a well-established role in recognizing and binding H3K9me2/3, facilitating the targeted recruitment and localization of HP1 to heterochromatic regions (Wang et al., 2019; Schoelz and Riddle, 2022; Maison and Almouzni, 2004; Lomberk et al., 2006a).
evidence: This is supported by cited references.

claim: The CD also facilitates multivalent electrostatic interactions governing the LLPS of human HP1 paralogs.
source: Our simulations suggest that the CD also facilitates multivalent electrostatic interactions governing the LLPS of human HP1 paralogs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from simulation data.

claim: The oligomerization mechanism of human HP1 paralogs appears to be distinct from the oligomerization capabilities of Swi6, which can promote multivalency through direct CD-CD interactions.
source: This mechanism, however, appears to be distinct from the oligomerization capabilities of Swi6 (Sanulli et al., 2019), which can promote multivalency through direct CD-CD interactions.
evidence: This is a comparison with cited work on Swi6.

claim: HP1α and HP1γ show common overlapping regions in heterochromatin but also distinct territories where only certain paralogs are enriched.
source: The nuclear localization patterns of HP1 paralogs (Lachner et al., 2001; Bannister et al., 2001; Maison and Almouzni, 2004) show that there are common overlapping regions in heterochromatin but also distinct territories where only certain paralogs are enriched, e.g., the presence of HP1γ and HP1β in euchromatin.
evidence: This is supported by cited references.

source: For example, in mixtures of HP1 paralog homodimers, the HP1α hinge region serves as a central hub, connecting adjacent paralogs through electrostatic attraction involving the NTE, CD, or CTE domains.

claim: HP1β can function as a client, partitioning into the HP1α scaffold condensate in a concentration-dependent manner.

source: Specifically, at low concentrations, HP1β can be directly recruited to the phase-separated droplet of HP1α, consistent with experimental observations (Larson et al., 2017).

claim: HP1γ can cooperatively phase-separate with HP1α due to preferential cross-interactions between its NTE/CD and the HP1α hinge region.

claim: HP1α-HP1β and HP1α-HP1γ heterodimers have a lower propensity to undergo LLPS compared to HP1α alone but display enhanced properties compared to HP1β and HP1γ homodimers, respectively.

claim: HP1α displays the most robust phase separation with DNA due to multiple attractive hotspots in the hinge, NTE, and CD.
source: HP1α displays the most robust phase separation with DNA due to multiple attractive hotspots in the hinge, NTE, and CD (Figure 5a and c).

claim: HP1γ interacts with DNA primarily through its extended positively charged NTE and through some conserved basic residue stretches in the hinge.
source: HP1γ interacts with DNA primarily through its extended positively charged NTE and through some conserved basic residue stretches in the hinge (Figure 5e).

claim: In HP1β, contacts with DNA are strongly disfavored due to the overall negative charge of its sequence and LLPS is not observed.

claim: When HP1α-DNA condensates are pre-formed and HP1β is subsequently added at equimolar concentration with HP1α, HP1β molecules mainly remain at the HP1α-DNA phase boundary.

claim: HP1γ preferentially interacts with DNA through its NTE and hinge and cooperatively phase separates with HP1α, thereby stabilizing pre-formed HP1α-DNA condensates.
source: In contrast, HP1γ preferentially interacts with DNA through its NTE and hinge and cooperatively phase separates with HP1α, thereby stabilizing pre-formed HP1α-DNA condensates (Figures 5e, 6c, d and h).

source: In this picture, HP1α is central in regulating DNA compaction and initiating protein condensation with DNA or upon phosphorylation.

claim: HP1γ preferentially enters and cooperatively enhances HP1α condensates, forming heterochromatic domains that silence DNA transactions.
source: HP1γ preferentially enters and cooperatively enhances HP1α condensates, forming heterochromatic domains that silence DNA transactions.

claim: The CG single homodimer simulations and the CG coexistence phase simulations were performed using the HPS-Urry model.
source: The CG single homodimer simulations and the CG coexistence phase simulations of HP1 proteins and HP1 proteins with DNA were performed in the HOOMD-Blue 2.9.7 software package (Anderson et al., 2020), using the protocol described in our previous studies (Dignon et al., 2018b; Regy et al., 2021b).
evidence: This is a methodological description.

claim: The proteins and DNA were modeled using the one-bead-per-residue HPS-Urry model and the recently developed two-bead-per-nucleotide DNA model, respectively.
source: The proteins and DNA were modeled using the one-bead-per-residue HPS-Urry model (Regy et al., 2021b) and the recently developed two-bead-per-nucleotide DNA model (Kapoor et al., 2024), respectively.
evidence: This is a methodological description.

claim: All CG simulations were conducted at 100 mM salt concentration.
source: All the CG simulations were conducted at 100 mM salt concentration.
evidence: This is a methodological description.

claim: All systems were simulated at 320 K to compare the phase separation propensities of homo- and heterodimers and their chimeras.
source: As the coexistence density in the dilute phase was too low at 300 K, we simulated all systems at 320 K to compare the phase separation propensities of homo- and heterodimers and their chimeras.
evidence: This is a methodological description.

claim: Atomistic simulations of HP1 paralogs were modeled using the force field Amber99SBws-STQ.
source: The system topologies were modeled using the force field Amber99SBws-STQ (Tang et al., 2020), which is available at https://bitbucket.org/jeetain/all-atom_ff_refinements (Phan, 2023).
evidence: This is a methodological description.
